title: A project's .decade/config.toml lays out its workspace
body:
A new workspace starts with one terminal (decade-4c2624). Jack wants a project to be able to describe its own layout.

## Proposal

- A project directory may hold `.decade/config.toml`, with a version key. It describes the split tree, with ratios, and for each pane a name and either a command or a plain shell, plus an optional cwd relative to the project.
- A new workspace for that directory starts from the template. Without one it gets a single terminal.
- The template runs commands from the project directory, so decade asks before using a template it has not seen. It remembers the answer by path and content hash, so a changed file asks again.
- "Save layout as template" in the palette writes the current workspace's tree into the project's file.

## Open

- Whether a global default template in `~/.config/decade` comes later.
